topics.title: Pattern overview
topics.summary: Add optional behavior around an individual object without writing one subclass for every feature combination. Worked example: Two ways to decorate a status message. Each wrapper owns exactly one Message and implements the same query. Ownership makes the assembled chain self-contained; explicit nesting makes order reviewable.

blocks.title: Learning objectives
items: Compose optional behavior around one shared interface.
Predict how wrapper order changes a result.
Own and destroy a chain of message objects safely.

blocks.text: Component defines the shared operation. A concrete component supplies the basic result. Each decorator implements that same contract and stores another Component connection. Calls travel inward through the wrapper chain; returned results travel outward and can be changed at each layer. The client chooses the order of the layers. Different orders may have different meanings, even when the component and wrapper types are identical.

cards.question: What problem does Decorator address?
cards.answer: Add optional behavior around an individual object without writing one subclass for every feature combination. Worked example: Two ways to decorate a status message. Each wrapper owns exactly one Message and implements the same query. Ownership makes the assembled chain self-contained; explicit nesting makes order reviewable.

cards.question: What is Decorator?
cards.answer: An object that adds behavior around another object while keeping the same interface.

cards.question: What is Noncommutative?
cards.answer: Describes operations whose result can change when their order is swapped.

cards.question: What is Idempotent?
cards.answer: Describes an operation whose repeated application has the same effect as applying it once.

cards.question: Why must inner_ have the Message interface rather than be fixed to Plain?
cards.answer: It must accept another decorator as well as Plain. Otherwise the wrappers cannot form arbitrary chains.

cards.question: Does Prefix(Limit(text)) mean the complete visible result is limited to five bytes?
cards.answer: No. Limit trims the inner text before Prefix adds its bytes. Put Limit outside Prefix to limit the complete visible result.

cards.question: Why does reversing two wrappers often change the result?
cards.answer: Each wrapper receives the result of its inner object. Limiting before adding text differs from limiting after adding it, so the composition is generally order-sensitive.

cards.question: Does Decorator require every wrapper to add characters?
cards.answer: No. Limit removes characters while keeping the Message interface. The common property is wrapping an object and changing behavior, not always increasing output size.

cards.question: Why are wrapper service objects nonmovable while their unique_ptr handles can move?
cards.answer: Moving the handle transfers ownership without relocating the service object. This preserves object identity and avoids supporting partially moved service states.

cards.question: Could one formatting function replace this wrapper graph?
cards.answer: Yes for a small fixed pipeline. Wrappers earn their cost when callers assemble and reorder optional behavior through a shared interface.

cards.question: Why should a null-inner check run during construction?
cards.answer: It prevents creating a wrapper that can never satisfy text(). Detecting the error at assembly time is clearer than crashing during a later render.

cards.question: How would byte limits differ from display-character limits?
cards.answer: std::string::substr counts bytes. A UTF-8 character can use several bytes, so a byte cut may split it. A display-text contract needs a suitable text-aware representation.

cards.question: What ownership action happens when the outermost wrapper is destroyed?
cards.answer: Its unique_ptr destroys the inner object, which destroys its own inner object in turn. Virtual destructors allow deletion through Message to reach the actual types.

topics.title: When two small features produce many variants
topics.summary: A status panel starts with plain text such as ready now. Some screens add WARN before the text. Some limit the display to five characters. A screen may need both behaviors, and its policy must say which applies first. For this chapter, strings contain simple single-byte characters. The program is not a full Unicode layout engine.

blocks.text: With one fixed policy, a direct expression is the simplest implementation. Add the prefix and take a substring. That clearly states the order. The problem appears when screens choose different combinations at runtime. Classes named PrefixedMessage, LimitedMessage, PrefixedLimitedMessage, and LimitedPrefixedMessage repeat pieces of behavior. Adding a suffix or a timestamp creates more combinations. We need reusable features that can be assembled without defining a new class for every pairing.

discussion.question: Why can adding a prefix before trimming text differ from adding it after trimming?
discussion.answer: Trimming the prefixed result can remove part of the original message or suffix. Trimming the original first leaves the later prefix outside the limit. Order is part of the requirement, not an implementation detail.

topics.title: A wrapper with the same public operation
topics.summary: A decorator is an object that adds behavior around another object while keeping the same interface. Message provides text(). Plain returns its stored text. Prefix and Limit are also Messages, but each owns an inner Message and calls that object's text before adding its own behavior. Since the inner object may itself be another decorator, the same construction rule supports a chain of features.

blocks.text: The important fact is that every layer remains usable as a Message. This is why the common interface is needed now: callers must accept an assembled chain without knowing its exact shape. Public inheritance supplies that substitutability. Containing an inner Message supplies the behavior being extended. The inheritance link and the ownership link answer different questions and must remain distinct in the diagram.

We do not add a generic Decorator base class merely to repeat the inner_ member. Two small wrappers do not yet need that additional inheritance layer. If many wrappers later share forwarding behavior and validation, a base wrapper can remove useful duplication. First show the repeated need; then judge whether sharing that implementation makes the code easier to change.

topics.title: Order is visible behavior
topics.summary: The first chain is Prefix around Limit around Plain. A call enters Prefix, which asks Limit for text. Limit asks Plain and receives ready now. Limit keeps the first five characters, ready, and returns them. Prefix then adds WARN and returns WARN ready. The five-character rule applied only to the inner body, so the final string is longer than five.

blocks.text: The second chain is Limit around Prefix around Plain. Plain again returns ready now. Prefix returns WARN ready now. The outer Limit keeps its first five characters: W, A, R, N, and a space. The printed single quotes make the trailing space visible. The final result is 'WARN '. This is not an implementation accident. The outermost operation runs last on the returned text in this design.

Operations whose order changes the result are noncommutative: swapping them changes behavior. Prefix and Limit are a concrete example. Never document a stack merely as 'prefix plus limit' if the order matters. Show the nesting or the actual transformation sequence. For logging, validation, caching, and compression wrappers in real systems, a wrong order can matter much more than a shortened message.

topics.title: Follow ownership separately from the call stack
topics.summary: Each wrapper stores unique_ptr<Message>. Its constructor receives an owner by value and moves that owner into inner_. The caller gives up ownership as part of construction. A null pointer is rejected immediately, so text can safely call inner_->text without a null check on every request. If construction throws, the already-initialized member owner cleans up its inner object automatically.

blocks.text: make_unique constructs each object and returns its owner. main nests those calls from the plain object outward. When first is destroyed, its Prefix is destroyed, which destroys its inner Limit, which destroys its Plain. Message has a virtual destructor so deleting through unique_ptr<Message> reaches the correct derived destructor. No caller needs to remember the chain's exact concrete types to clean it up.

During text(), each layer also creates local strings. body receives the inner result by value; result stores this layer's transformed text. These values own their character storage, so the method never returns a reference to a local string. Returning a string value permits safe transfer of the result to the caller. The chain's object lifetime is much longer than each local string's lifetime, and the two should not be confused.

Message explicitly allows default construction but deletes copy and move construction and assignment. The = delete notation asks the compiler to reject those operations. Derived wrappers therefore cannot be moved as whole objects, which would empty inner_ in the source and violate its non-null rule. Move the owning unique_ptr handle instead: ownership changes hands while the wrapper object and its inner chain stay in place. Compile-time static_assert checks use the type traits from <type_traits> to verify that Prefix and Limit cannot be copied or moved. The Suffix solution checks the same property. A type trait is a library query about a type; static_assert rejects a false condition during compilation.

topics.title: Syntax, cost, and boundary assumptions
topics.summary: The compiler verifies that every concrete Message implements text() const with the right return type. override makes the check explicit. const permits reading through a const Message reference and promises not to alter the object through that method's ordinary members. It does not automatically make an arbitrary chain thread-safe if future decorators introduce mutable caches or shared services.

blocks.text: At execution, virtual dispatch chooses each layer and each layer delegates once. substr(0, limit_) begins at position zero and takes at most limit_ characters. If the requested length is larger than the body, it returns the whole body. A zero limit returns an empty string. std::size_t is an unsigned size type; a negative signed value converted to it would become a large positive size. The program constructs limits from nonnegative literals, and a user-input interface would need to reject negative values before conversion.

A chain with many layers may allocate and copy many intermediate strings. This example favors clarity over a claim of best performance. A fixed transformation pipeline made of ordinary functions can be simpler and cheaper when callers do not need objects sharing an interface. A streaming design may avoid large intermediates, but then each layer must define how it handles partial input and failures.

Decorator is useful when features are independently selectable and have a consistent component contract. It is less useful when the features depend on many details of one another or when an object needs a radically different interface. Keep the assembly code readable, test the important orders, and document whether repeated decoration is meaningful. Applying Prefix twice adds two prefixes; it is not automatically idempotent, meaning it does not necessarily leave the result unchanged after the first application.

items: Every wrapper has one non-null inner owner.

blocks.text: Alternative: A pair of string functions is better for one fixed transformation sequence. A vector of transformation functions fits a pipeline that does not otherwise need a Message object interface.

topics.title: Exercise 09.3: Diagnose a bug
topics.summary: A developer returns body.substr(limit_, 0) from Limit. What does it return for body="ready" and limit_=2, and why is that wrong?

blocks.title: Hint
blocks.text: The arguments are start position and requested count.

blocks.title: Explained answer
blocks.text: It returns an empty string because the count is zero. The requirement was the first two characters, re. Use body.substr(0, limit_). With a start beyond body.size(), the wrong version can also throw out_of_range.

workshop.title: Two ways to decorate a status message
workshop.problem: Two ways to decorate a status message. Support plain text, prefixing, and a length limit. Permit either wrapper order through Message::text. Reject a wrapper with no inner object and preserve empty-string behavior.
workshop.output:
prefix outside: 'WARN ready'
limit outside: 'WARN '
empty and missing-inner checks passed

steps.why: The leaf owns the original text.

steps.state: inner Limit -> ready; outer Prefix -> WARN ready
steps.why: Only the body is limited in first.

steps.state: inner Prefix -> WARN ready now; outer Limit -> WARN
steps.why: The entire decorated result is limited in second.

steps.state: outer owner destroyed -> inner owners destroyed
steps.why: The chain of unique_ptr members releases each component once.

workshop.pitfall: Assume Prefix(Limit(text)) and Limit(Prefix(text)) are equivalent. The first produces WARN ready, the second WARN plus a trailing space. The limit acts on different intermediate strings.

discussion.question: A command always performs exactly prefix then limit and is not passed as a Message. Choose decorators or direct string functions.
discussion.answer: Use direct functions or a single clearly named function. Decorator adds useful structure when features are independently configured as Message objects, but a fixed two-step operation does not need a heap-owned class chain.

workshop.alternative: A pair of string functions is better for one fixed transformation sequence. A vector of transformation functions fits a pipeline that does not otherwise need a Message object interface.
workshop.design: Each wrapper owns exactly one Message and implements the same query. Ownership makes the assembled chain self-contained; explicit nesting makes order reviewable.
invariants: Every wrapper has one non-null inner owner.
text returns a new value and does not mutate the chain.
Limit applies to the complete result returned by its immediate inner object.
workshop.maintenance: Middleware and formatting layers use the same principle: keep feature contracts small, make order explicit, and test combinations that may interact.
workshop.verification: Both wrapper orders are checked, together with empty Plain text, zero limit, an oversized limit, and a rejected missing inner object. The example makes no promise about Unicode grapheme boundaries or allocation performance. Compile-time type traits verify that Prefix and Limit object copying and moving are disabled; ownership handles remain movable.
